task: T1: create scripts/gate-selftest.sh with its argument handling and its hermetic workspace, and nothing else. It takes one argument, the path to a task directory — the kind holding a `verify.sh` and a `mutants/` subdirectory. Refuse with a clear message and a non-zero exit when the argument is missing, when the directory does not exist, when it holds no `verify.sh`, or when it holds no `mutants/` directory; each of those is a different message naming what was wrong, because a tool that says only "usage" makes the caller guess which of four things it got wrong. Then build the workspace: copy the repository into a temp directory and do all subsequent work there. It must never write inside the repository it was pointed at — several specs in this repo assert that files outside their own scope are untouched, so a self-test that leaves a mutant behind fails an unrelated spec's gate and looks like someone else's bug. Remove the temp directory when the script exits, including on failure. In this task the script does nothing after building the workspace except exit zero; T2 parses mutants and T3 runs them. Write `return 0` explicitly at the end of any function whose last construct is a loop or a conditional: a function inherits the exit status of its last construct, and for a loop that is its terminating condition, which is reliably non-zero — this exact trap silently killed every run of the previous spec's implementation.
